metadata.title: System security plan: cicd demo guestbook
metadata.remarks: Generated from the profile and the platform, app and sysadmin layers. Leveraged authorizations (a platform SSP) are a later step.

system-characteristics.description: A Flask guestbook used to demonstrate cicd-ref-arch; entries are kept in memory only.

information-types.title: Guestbook entries
information-types.description: Names and short messages typed in by visitors; not persisted, lost when the app scales to zero.

authorization-boundary.description: The demo's dev, branch and prod environments on c-local, built and deployed by cicd-ref-arch.

components.title: cicd demo guestbook
components.description: A Flask guestbook used to demonstrate cicd-ref-arch; entries are kept in memory only.

components.title: cicd-ref-arch pipeline (build, scan, gate, deploy, promote)
components.description: Every push is tested, built, scanned (gitleaks, opengrep, checkov, syft, grype), gated by policy and deployed from git; prod changes only through a two-person promotion that re-scans the image.

components.title: demo, as operated by its owner
components.description: What the demo's owner does around the pipeline.

control-implementation.description: Objective-level statements per layer; status from coverage.

by-components.description:
cm-2_obj.a-1: The rendered manifests and the image digest of every environment are written to git by the pipeline.
cm-2_obj.a-2: The baseline changes only through commits (app repo, then state repo); images are pinned by digest.
cm-2_obj.b.3: Installing or upgrading a component is a commit, which re-renders and re-records the baseline.

cm-2_obj.b.1: The baseline (manifests, base image digests, pinned dependencies) is reviewed at every promotion and at least quarterly.
cm-2_obj.b.2: The baseline is reviewed after a security advisory affecting it, and when the platform changes its floor.

cm-8_obj.a.1: syft inventories the built image itself, so the inventory is what runs.
cm-8_obj.a.2: The SBOM covers every package in the image (OS and language packages).
cm-8_obj.a.3: One SBOM per image digest, per application; nothing is shared or counted twice.
cm-8_obj.a.4: Package level, with purl, version and licence (CycloneDX and SPDX).
cm-8_obj.a.5: Each component has name, version, purl and licence where the package declares one.
cm-8_obj.b: The inventory is regenerated on every build, and re-checked daily against new advisories.

ra-5_obj.a-1: The SBOM of every live image is re-matched when the vulnerability database updates (daily) or an advisory arrives.
ra-5_obj.a-2: Every push is scanned; prod is re-scanned at promotion request and again at apply.
ra-5_obj.b.1: Scanning, normalisation and the gate decision are automatic, per commit.
ra-5_obj.b.2: Findings are normalised to one record format with CVE ids and purls (security-findings/v1).
ra-5_obj.b.3: Configuration is checked with checkov's rule set and code with opengrep rules kept in git.
ra-5_obj.c: Each finding gets an outcome (fail, suppressed with reason and expiry, below threshold, no fix) in the gate record.
ra-5_obj.d: A vulnerability with a fix blocks prod until it is fixed or recorded as not affecting the app.
ra-5_obj.e: The owner releases assessment packages to IT Security from the dashboard (release log in the compliance repo).
ra-5_obj.f: grype's database is refreshed daily and its build time is recorded with every scan.
sa-11_obj.a-1: The assessment plan is this SSP's evidence selectors, kept in git and reviewed with the owner.

sa-11_obj.a-2: The pipeline runs the security assessment on every commit of every branch.
sa-11_obj.b: Unit tests and static, configuration, secret and vulnerability scans on every commit.
sa-11_obj.c-1: Each job writes a ci-result/v1 record; the run log is kept by the forge.
sa-11_obj.c-2: Results are recorded per commit next to the environment they produced.
sa-11_obj.d: Suppressions need a reason and an expiry, are versioned with the code, and show as a diff in every promotion.
sa-11_obj.e: Findings at or above the threshold block prod until corrected.

si-2_obj.a-1: Flaws are identified by the scans of every commit and by imported findings.
si-2_obj.a-2: Flaws are reported in the run, the gate record and the dashboard.
si-2_obj.a-3: Flaws that block prod are corrected before promotion.
si-2_obj.b-1: A fix is a commit; it is tested before it is deployed anywhere.
si-2_obj.b-2: The same tests run on the fix, in a dev or branch environment before prod.
si-2_obj.b-3: not applicable: Containers carry no firmware; host firmware belongs to the hosting system's plan (leveraged).
si-2_obj.b-4: not applicable: Containers carry no firmware; host firmware belongs to the hosting system's plan (leveraged).
si-2_obj.c-1: Security updates with a fix block prod until installed (rebuilt and promoted).
si-2_obj.c-2: not applicable: Containers carry no firmware; host firmware belongs to the hosting system's plan (leveraged).
si-2_obj.d: Every fix is a commit through the same pipeline and promotion as any change.
ia-5.7_obj: gitleaks on every commit, and the forge refuses pushes that add a secret (pre-receive hook).
